topic.subject: science
topic.title: Sound waves
topic.scope: longitudinal waves, compressions and rarefactions, wavelength, frequency, speed of sound, echo, ultrasound

misconceptions.statement: Sound can travel through a vacuum.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate light and sound because both are perceived as waves.
misconceptions.fix: Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a material medium like air, water, or solids to propagate.

probe.question: If a bell rings inside a glass jar from which all air has been removed, will you hear it?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because sound waves can travel through empty space.

misconceptions.statement: Sound is a physical object that moves from the source to the ear.
misconceptions.why: Everyday language like 'the sound hit me' suggests sound is a projectile or a substance.
misconceptions.fix: Sound is a disturbance or energy transfer that causes particles of the medium to vibrate in place.

probe.question: Does the air you breathe at the source of a sound actually travel to your ear?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, the air molecules move all the way from the speaker to my ear.

misconceptions.statement: Sound waves move up and down like water waves.
misconceptions.why: Textbooks often use transverse wave diagrams to represent all waves, leading to visual confusion.
misconceptions.fix: Sound waves are longitudinal, meaning particles oscillate back and forth in the same direction the wave travels.

probe.question: In which direction do air particles move when a sound wave passes through them?
probe.wrong_answer: They move up and down perpendicular to the direction of the sound.

misconceptions.statement: Loud sounds have a higher frequency than quiet sounds.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the intensity (loudness) with the pitch (frequency) of a sound.
misconceptions.fix: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the wave, while pitch depends on the frequency.

probe.question: If you shout louder, what happens to the pitch of your voice?
probe.wrong_answer: The pitch gets higher because the sound is louder.

misconceptions.statement: Sound travels at the same speed regardless of the material.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume sound is a constant property of the 'sound' itself rather than the medium.
misconceptions.fix: The speed of sound depends on the properties of the medium, such as density and elasticity, and is fastest in solids.

probe.question: Does sound travel faster through steel or through air?
probe.wrong_answer: It travels at the same speed in both because sound is constant.
